notes.heading: Separate signed displacement from total distance
paragraphs: The area under a velocity-time graph is signed displacement. Motion in the opposite direction contributes negative area, while distance adds the magnitudes of all segments. A zero final displacement can therefore accompany substantial travel. Average speed divides total distance by elapsed time; average velocity divides displacement by the same interval. Force determines acceleration in the constant-mass Newtonian model, not the direction of velocity itself. A nonzero velocity can persist with zero resultant force, and a force opposing velocity can slow an object without immediately reversing it.

questions.prompt: An idealised trolley moves at +3 m/s for 4 s, then at -2 m/s for 6 s. Ignore the brief change of velocity. Find displacement, distance and average speed.
questions.answer: Displacement 0 m, distance 24 m, average speed 2.4 m/s.
solution: Signed displacements are +12 m and -12 m.
Add magnitudes for distance and divide by total time 10 s.

questions.prompt: A 5 kg object moves right at constant velocity on a horizontal surface. A 12 N rightward force acts. Assuming only one other horizontal force, find it and explain your reasoning.
questions.answer: The other horizontal force is 12 N leftward.
solution: Newton's second law therefore requires zero resultant horizontal force.

questions.prompt: An object starts at velocity +4 m/s and maintains acceleration -2 m/s² for 4 s. Find when it reverses direction, its displacement and total distance.
questions.answer: It reverses after 2 s; displacement is 0 m and distance is 8 m.
solution: Use v=4-2t to locate v=0 at t=2 s.
The velocity-time graph gives equal signed triangle areas +4 and -4 m.
markingPoints: Add triangle magnitudes to obtain distance 8 m.
